 The Gilded Age returns to HBO for Season 4, premiering Sunday, November 1 at 9 p.m. ET.
 To celebrate the momentous occasion, the cast of the HBO period drama reunited in New York City with creator Julian Fellowes in attendance.
 The new season of the period drama will see the Russells reckon with the consequences as Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) seizes a chance to regain her position. Meanwhile, Marian (Louisa Jacobson) forges a new path for herself, and Peggy (Denée Benton) works to earn acceptance from her future in-laws. In this new era, you must be careful what you wish for.
 RELATED: Bravo Fan Fest: Charleston Photos: Andy Cohen, Porsha Williams, Madison LeCroy, Lisa Barlow, Ava Dash & More 
 Season 4’s cast includes Carrie Coon, Christine Baranski, Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Louisa Jacobson, Denée Benton, Taissa Farmiga, Harry Richardson, Blake Ritson, Ben Ahlers, Ashlie Atkinson, Dylan Baker, Kelley Curran, Jordan Donica, Jessica Frances Dukes, Amy Forsyth, and Jack Gilpin.
 Also part of the HBO series is Simon Jones, Celia Keenan-Bolger, Ben Lamb, Audra McDonald, Brian Stokes Mitchell, Debra Monk, Hattie Morahan, Donna Murphy, Kristine Nielsen, Kelli O’Hara, Taylor Richardson, Douglas Sills, Erin Wilhelmi, John Douglas Thompson, Taylor Trensch, James Scully, Dennis Haysbert, Maggie Kuntz, Neal Huff, Bonnie Milligan, Jim Gaffigan, Dallas Roberts, Andrew Burnap, Elizabeth Marvel, Adrienne Warren, with Bill Camp and Phylicia Rashad.
 RELATED: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’: New Photos Of Film Starring Brad Pitt, Elizabeth Debicki, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II & More 
 Julian Fellowes is the creator of  The Gilded Age and also a writer and executive producer. The creative team also includes Salli Richardson-Whitfield (director and EP) and Sonja Warfield (writer and EP). The series’s executive producers are Gareth Neame, David Crockett, Bob Greenblatt, Kate Churchill, Davita Scarlett, and Elaine Aronson; co-executive producers are Erica Armstrong Dunbar and Holly Rymon.
 The Gilded Age is a co-production between HBO and Universal Television, a division of Universal Studio Group.
